subject: Using sendInputMessage and receiveMessage to make shiny input objects reactive

messages.author: f6dea426c8b7a030
messages.subject: Using sendInputMessage and receiveMessage to make shiny input objects reactive
parts:
Smart people, your help is needed!

As pointed out here,
   https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/oAqYY4thV94
the update functions provide a way to change shiny input objects,
which are ordinarily not reactive.  So you can make their appearance reactive
like shiny output objects. 

The update functions use session$sendInputMessage
to communicate with a javascript "receiveMessage" function in the input binding
for the object you want to modify.

I wrote a receiveMessage function for the ss-jstree class in the shinysky package,
to update reactively when the tree's data object changes.
That works fine, but then the ability to select a node in the tree vanishes.
Something about the binding is out of sync.
More details from the jstree angle are here:
   https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/jstree/xHp6JWssWOI

The new tree has the same id as the old tree.
It has the wrong classes, but if I fix the classes by hand,
that's not enough;
the responsiveness to a node click is not restored.
Same id, correct class names, but no longer working.

So there's something deep about input binding that I'm not getting.

messages.author: f6dea426c8b7a030
messages.subject: Re: Using sendInputMessage and receiveMessage to make shiny input objects reactive
parts:
I solved this problem with the help of Ivan the jstree guru.
I'd been confused between different jstree  versions.

There is only one way currently to make a jstree version 3.0 
reactive (in the javascript, not R shiny, sense),
by creating the jstree with a core:data clause:
 $("#jstreeScenario").jstree(
{ core: { data: function(node, cb) { cb(theJsonMessage); }},
       ...
);
Then from R use session$sendInputMessage 
to send the tree's new JSON into the javascript receiver,
where you get
$.extend(ss_jstree, {
  receiveMessage: function(el, inputMessage) {
    message = inputMessage;
    // clean up the message
    message = message.replace(/..."is.logical..."/g, "is.logical");
    message = message.replace(/..."is.numeric..."/g, "is.numeric");
    message = message.replace(/\\"/g, '"');
    message = message.replace(/'/g, "");
    message = message.replace(/^ *\[1\] *"/, "");
    message = message.replace(/.$/, "");
    theJsonMessage = eval(message);
...

After assigning to theJsonMessage, the tree appearance automatically refreshes.
This is working now in ClinicalTrialDesignExperimenter.
The message cleanup is needed to make sure various special characters
don't mess up the JSON; the details will depend on what non-alphanumeric characters 
appear in your tree. The cleanup you see above is fine for my stuff;
I'm sure it's not sufficient for all cases.

I've left out some details, like how to assemble the message to pass 
via session$sendInputMessage.
If interested, refer to ClinicalTrialDesignExperimenter on github,
and check out these files inside the folder  inst/shinyInterface/:
    jstreeScenarioContent.html 
    www.ss-jstree.js
    ui.R  & search for jstreeScenario
    server.R & search for observerCurrentScenario


I'm not really using shinysky's jstree,
but my customized version which was inspired by it. (Thanks, Xiaodaigh.)
The shinyTree package is now at cran, I think,
and maybe it solves these problems, but too late for me.
